metadata.title: Simple Harmonic Motion Is Circular Motion Seen Edge-On
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: What does a block on a spring have in common with a peg on a spinning wheel?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A block oscillates on a spring, while a peg rides the rim of a wheel turning at constant speed. One moves back and forth along a line, the other goes around a circle. Yet they are doing the same thing.
beats.new_visual_element: Top: a grey wheel turning counterclockwise at constant angular speed, with a gold peg on its rim. Bottom: a red block on a grey zigzag spring attached to a wall, oscillating left and right on a floor line.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: spinning wheel with peg above, block-spring oscillator below

beats.narration_text: Shine a light from directly above, so the peg casts a shadow on a horizontal axis. If the wheel has radius A, the shadow slides back and forth between plus A and minus A, slowing at the ends and moving fastest through the center.
beats.new_visual_element: A horizontal axis below the wheel with ticks at -A, 0, +A; a dashed vertical projection line from the peg down to the axis, tracked every frame; a gold shadow dot where it lands.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: wheel, peg, projection line, shadow dot on the axis, block-spring below

beats.narration_text: Now look at the block beneath it. When the wheel turns at an angular frequency omega equal to two pi times the block's oscillation frequency, the shadow stays on the block at every instant: same position, same speed, same turning points.
beats.new_visual_element: The projection line extends down to the block; a copy of the shadow dot drops onto the block's center and rides with it. Both the shadow and the block pulse with an outline at each turning point, together. Label ω = 2πf.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: wheel, projection line through axis to block, shadow and block moving in lockstep, ω = 2πf

beats.narration_text: The peg's angle grows steadily, theta equals omega t, so the shadow's position is the projection of the radius: x equals A cos omega t. Recorded over time, that position traces a cosine curve, the signature of simple harmonic motion.
beats.new_visual_element: A radius line from the wheel's center to the peg with a growing angle arc θ = ωt; equation x(t) = A cos(ωt); a chart-recorder trace below the block records the block's position with time running downward, drawing a cosine curve.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: wheel with angle θ, projection line, synchronized block, scrolling cosine trace, x(t) = A cos ωt

beats.narration_text: Simple harmonic motion is not a separate kind of movement. It is uniform circular motion, viewed edge-on.
beats.new_visual_element: Everything keeps moving in sync; summary line 'SHM = circular motion, viewed edge-on'.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame, still in motion
